topic: Hot take: AI labs grading their own homework isn't enough anymore
post:
An AI company rated its own new models "Critical" for cybersecurity risk.
Then it released them. 🔥

Here's what happened:
OpenAI launched GPT-6.2 Astra and GPT-6.2 Sol on Nov 17. According to coverage of OpenAI's system card (its safety report), both models were assessed as "Critical" for cybersecurity under the company's own Preparedness Framework.

The system card also notes that the UK's AI Security Institute had not independently retested the latest safeguards when it was written. 🧪

My hot take 👇
I'm not saying the release was wrong. Labs publish these reports, and that's good.

But when the same company builds the model, grades the risk, and decides it's safe to ship, that's grading your own homework. 📝

For the most powerful AI, independent testing before release should be the norm, not a nice-to-have.

Why it matters:
The AI tools you use at work are getting more capable every month. Who checks them, and when, matters as much as what they can do. ⚖️

Practical takeaway:
Before your team adopts a new AI model, read the vendor's safety report summary. Look for who tested it, not just what it scored. 🔍
